name: Pangai
note: Town: administrative capital village of Haʻapai on Lifuka, with the harbour, the Catholic church, a few shops and the group's main services; the base for visitors (Wikivoyage Haʻapai).

name: Lifuka
note: Island: the main island of Haʻapai, with Lifuka Island Airport and Pangai; the gateway and base for the group (Wikivoyage Haʻapai).

name: Shirley Baker Grave
note: Monument: grave and monument of Methodist missionary and prime minister Shirley Baker (died Pangai 1903), in the European cemetery in Pangai.

name: Lotofoa Methodist Church
note: Religious building: Methodist church named by Wikivoyage for its beautifully carved coconut-wood ceiling (interior visitors go in for).

name: Pangai Free Wesleyan Church
note: Religious building: Free Wesleyan church in Pangai, listed by the tourism board under Culture; interior and exterior not described.

name: Sangata Teleisia o Avila
note: Religious building: striking Catholic church in Pangai on Lifuka, listed by the tourism board under Culture.

name: Mystery Cross
note: Monument: a spiritual landmark cross in Pangai, Haʻapai, listed by the tourism board as a free activity.

name: Poseidon's Gate
note: Natural site: great rock terraces on the east side of Lifuka that Wikivoyage names as a stop.

name: Foa Petroglyphs
note: Historic site: ancient petroglyphs discovered at the northern end of Foa Island (Wikivoyage Haʻapai).

name: Foa Island
note: Island: small island joined to Lifuka by a concrete causeway, with the petroglyphs, Matafonua Lodge and the Port-au-Prince wreck offshore (Wikivoyage).

name: Port-au-Prince Wreck
note: Dive site: wreck of the British ship Port-au-Prince, sunk off Foa in the early 19th century (Wikivoyage Haʻapai): diving site rather than a land stop.

name: ʻUiha
note: Island: a short boat ride southwest of Pangai, the royal burial grounds with burial pyramids (Wikivoyage Haʻapai).

name: Tofua
note: Volcano: active volcanic island with a caldera crater lake; a boat trip and steep one-hour climb gives views of the crater (Wikivoyage: needs planning and is expensive).

name: Kao
note: Volcano: Tonga's highest point, a dormant stratovolcano reached by small boat to its south coast, with no paths to the summit (tourism board lists it under land adventures).

name: Uoleva
note: Island: secluded island just south of Pangai, reached on foot at low tide (potentially dangerous), with a beach and eco-retreat; tourism board calls it a secluded paradise.

name: Luahoko Island
note: Island: tiny uninhabited island with white sand beaches and palms, a Robinson Crusoe-type stop reached by day trip from nearby islands (Wikivoyage Haʻapai).

name: Kau Vai
note: Island trip: islet off Haʻano on the island-trip list in Wikivoyage Haʻapai; no visitor facilities named.

name: Tatafa
note: Island trip: islet on the island-trip list in Wikivoyage Haʻapai; day trip only, no visitor facilities named.
